harnessDefects.observed: Reported {totalErrors:0, verdict:"clean"} for a tree with 66 syntax errors in scope. It also reported both recorded baseline errors as "no longer present", printing a false "shared code changed" warning.
harnessDefects.cause: It parses tsc stdout with /\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - the PLAIN format. tsc in this repo emits PRETTY ANSI output even when not attached to a TTY: "file:LINE:COL - \x1b[...error\x1b[... TS1005". The regex matches zero lines for any input, so the tool always returns clean. ANSI escapes also split the literal "error TS", so even a naive grep misses it.
harnessDefects.fix: pass --pretty false to tsc (verified: 97 errors surface, correctly attributed by run folder)
harnessDefects.note: This is the exact failure mode pipeline-defects.md warns about: "A check that never fires is indistinguishable from a broken one." The harness README claims every checker was verified against a deliberately bad input; this one is not, or TS/flags changed since.

harnessVerified.result: WORKS - negative-controlled in this run: injecting --sl-color-does-not-exist-xyz and font: var(--sl-text-new-body-md) produced one missing and one shorthandTrap, then reverted and re-verified clean.

designSystemDefects.issue: Only variant="primary" sets --_bg-color: transparent for fill=ghost/outline. Every other variant (default/secondary, success, warning, danger, info, inverted) keeps --sl-color-background-secondary-bold, so a ghost or outline link still paints a solid block. There is no component for a bare inline text link.

avatar.css hides the subheader slot outright at size sm AND md, and md is the only size whose picture is 32px (--sl-size-400). A 32px avatar WITH a subheader - what this design draws - is not expressible. lg costs +8px of circle.

The :host background did not take effect in this composition: --_background resolved to #ffae00 but computed background-color stayed rgba(0,0,0,0) and the colour stayed the inherited --sl-color-foreground-plain. Had to be set from the parent.

Malformed in EVERY theme, not just itslearning: two offsets and no blur. A4 recorded it as an itslearning fault; the first 3,780 lines of theme.css are byte-identical across themes, so it is a core defect.

designSystemDefects.severity: bounds text fidelity for every run under these themes
designSystemDefects.issue: The CORE token hardcodes the literal 'Open Sans' while the BRAND layer of the SAME file declares --sl-brand-text-new-*-fontFamily: 'open-sans' - the Typekit face that actually loads (document.fonts reports open-sans|loaded). The core token does not reference the brand token, so the correctly-named face is defined and never used. Colours indirect through the brand layer correctly; families do not. Result: every text node in every run under itslearning or my-digital-book renders in the browser default fallback, measured here on the h1 (computed family 'Open Sans', no matching loaded face).

threeFrameComparison.conclusion: A4 and B agree more often than either agrees with A11, but the obvious reading - that 1280 vs 360 explains it - is wrong: the disagreements are in the DATA CONTRACT, which the viewport does not touch. The cause is that nothing carries a decision from one frame to the next.
threeFrameComparison.sharperThanTheA1Pair: The A1/B-Kampus pair MINTED THE SAME TAG from the same source component, so the collision was at least detectable. Here all three namespaces differ, so nothing collides and nothing is detectable - three incompatible AppHeaders coexist silently, and the first goal of the effort (Figma and code mapping identically) fails with no symptom.
threeFrameComparison.a4GroupsTableOverlap: NONE. A4 owns a groups-table; this screen has no table at all - the Students tab holds a form and an empty state. The anticipated overlap does not exist.
